newsitem.title: USA: Northrop to cut 1,100 workers, take $90 million charge.
newsitem.headline: Northrop to cut 1,100 workers, take $90 million charge.

text.p: Northrop Grumman Corp. said Wednesday it will close four plants and cut about 1,100 workers as part of a restructuring.
The nation's fifth largest defence contractor also said it would take a charge of $90 million in the fourth quarter for the moves, which were meant to streamline operations and stay competitive.
While the company will lay off about 1,100 workers, newly created jobs at some plants will reduce the net number of jobs lost to 755, the company said.

"We regret that these actions will result in the loss of jobs, but they are necessary if we are to meet the affordability demands of our customers and win new business," Chairman Kent Kresa said in a statement.
The brunt of the cuts will be felt in California, New York and Florida. The plants to be closed are in Hawthorne, Calif., Great River on Long Island, N.Y., Stuart, Fla., and Perry, Ga.
The $90 million charge includes $60 million for closing the plants and $30 million related to the job cuts and other one-time costs.
Northrop stock fell 37.5 cents to $77.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
